clue.text: Remnant, keepsake close to heart

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so only its final letter is kept

blocks.note: a relic is something kept in memory of the past
the final letter of heart

explanation.surface: A sentimental token, all that is left of a love, kept pressed near the heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'close to heart' looks like a tender phrase, but it means the last letter of heart.
explanation.definitionFit: A relict is a survivor or leftover, especially a species or feature surviving from an earlier era.

clue.text: Live on edge

blocks.note: RE means 'on the subject of'
a side is an edge or border

explanation.surface: Someone living precariously, always on the edge.
explanation.definitionFit: To reside somewhere is to live there as one's home; the two verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Boulanger playing in part of hotel, perhaps

indicators.note: playing with something means toying with it, so its letters are moved about

blocks.note: the surname taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: The composer or teacher Boulanger performing in a hotel's function room.
explanation.walkthrough: Nadia Boulanger was a famous French music teacher, which makes 'playing' read naturally as performing.
explanation.definitionFit: A lounge bar is the more comfortable bar room found in a pub or hotel; 'perhaps' admits it is an example.

clue.text: Cold month, mostly, in Bay of Naples island

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

blocks.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap
a month of the year

explanation.surface: A chilly spell in the Bay of Naples during most of a month.
explanation.definitionFit: Capri is the island famous for its Blue Grotto, lying at the mouth of the Bay of Naples.

clue.text: Cola - a cup drunk in Mexican resort

indicators.note: something drunk is tipsy and staggers out of order

blocks.note: the words taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: A tourist sips a cup of cola at a Mexican beach resort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' reads as the past tense of drink, matching the cola; here it means tipsy.
explanation.definitionFit: Acapulco is a well-known Pacific coast holiday resort city in Mexico.

clue.text: Forge iron bar originally on it

blocks.note: a bar in a pub is its counter; 'originally' puts it at the start
Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
it taken as written, with iron placed on top of it in this down clue

explanation.surface: A blacksmith working an iron bar at the forge.
explanation.walkthrough: Forge looks like the smithy's noun but is the verb meaning to fake.
explanation.definitionFit: To forge documents or money is to counterfeit them, making a fraudulent copy.

clue.text: Sportswear, and more feminine, belonging to us

blocks.note: plus means and more besides
F is the abbreviation for feminine
ours is the possessive for us

explanation.surface: A boast that our sportswear range also includes more for women.
explanation.walkthrough: Plus fours are baggy knee-length trousers traditionally worn for golf.
explanation.definitionFit: Plus fours are loose breeches once standard golfing and shooting attire, so they are sportswear.

clue.text: Solicit in entrance

blocks.note: first meaning: to press politicians for support
second meaning: an entrance hall or vestibule

explanation.surface: Someone touting for business in a doorway.
explanation.walkthrough: The verb sense comes from campaigners waiting in the lobby of Parliament to buttonhole members.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for seeking political influence and a noun for an entrance hall.

clue.text: Shed tears after blooming protest

blocks.note: flowers that are out are in bloom
to cry is to shed tears

explanation.surface: Someone weeping after a flowering, perhaps from hay fever, then complaining.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' places the weeping word behind the blooming one.
explanation.definitionFit: An outcry is a loud public protest or expression of objection.

clue.text: End of play is completely perplexing

blocks.note: first meaning: the close of a day's play in cricket
second meaning: baffles utterly

explanation.surface: A theatregoer finds the final act of a drama baffling.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, stumps is called when the umpires end the day's play by removing the bails; 'play' suggests theatre instead.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun names cricket's close of play, and the verb means baffles, so both senses fit one word.

clue.text: Copper - check it in chemical vessel

blocks.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
to curb is to check or restrain
taken as written

explanation.surface: A lab instruction: put copper in a flask and check it.
explanation.definitionFit: A cucurbit is the gourd-shaped lower part of an alembic, a vessel used in distillation.

clue.text: Pet using force digging out new plant

indicators.note: digging something out removes it, so that letter is taken away

blocks.note: a dog is the classic pet
violent means using force
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A dog forcibly digging up a freshly planted flower.
explanation.walkthrough: The dog digging up a plant is a convincing picture; 'digging out' removes the N from the forceful word.
explanation.definitionFit: The dog violet is a common unscented wild violet of woods and hedgerows.

clue.text: Ably matched, surprisingly, in a Shakespearean role

indicators.note: something that turns out surprisingly comes out in an unexpected form

blocks.note: the words taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: A review praising an actor unexpectedly well cast in a Shakespeare part.
explanation.definitionFit: Lady Macbeth is the scheming wife who goads her husband to murder in Macbeth, a famous stage part.

clue.text: In favour of retaining the old entrance hallway

indicators.note: retaining means holding on to, so one piece is kept inside another

blocks.note: for means in favour of
ye is an archaic spelling of the

explanation.surface: Someone who prefers keeping a period entrance hall in an old house.
explanation.walkthrough: YE as old 'the' comes from shop signs like 'Ye Olde Tea Shoppe'.
explanation.definitionFit: A foyer is the entrance hall of a theatre, hotel or house, so the terms are synonyms.

clue.text: Makes a faux pas plugging bishop, American, with old handgun

indicators.note: plugging a gap means stuffing something into it, so these pieces go inside

blocks.note: to blunder is to make a faux pas
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
US is short for American

explanation.surface: A clumsy social gaffe involving a bishop, an American and an antique pistol.
explanation.walkthrough: A blunderbuss was a short flintlock gun with a flared muzzle; the surface's bishop is only the chess abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A blunderbuss is a short flared-muzzle firearm of the 1600s and 1700s, an early gun.

clue.text: Slaughtering centaur popular? Not sure

indicators.note: slaughtering something butchers it, so its letters are cut up and rearranged

blocks.note: taken letter for letter
something in is fashionable and popular

explanation.surface: A doubtful voter wonders whether killing a mythical horse-man would be a vote-winner.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram fodder is centaur plus the two-letter word for popular, shuffled together.
explanation.definitionFit: Uncertain means doubtful, without conviction, so it is a direct synonym of not sure.

clue.text: Criticism of face-lift?

blocks.note: surface reading: a disparaging comment about cosmetic surgery
setter's reading: a cosmetic operation is a quick wipe of the cheeks, so an indirect, glancing jab of criticism

explanation.surface: Someone sneering at another's cosmetic surgery.
explanation.walkthrough: The face's sides are its cheeks; giving them a swipe sounds like a face treatment, while the answer is an incidental critical remark.
explanation.definitionFit: A sideswipe is a passing or indirect critical remark made while talking about something else.

clue.text: Nobbled proceeds - men indemnified

indicators.note: something nobbled has been tampered with, so the letters are interfered with and rearranged

blocks.note: the words taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: Crooks who rigged a race and pocketed the takings are covered against loss.
explanation.walkthrough: To nobble is British slang for tampering with a racehorse or bribing a juror.
explanation.definitionFit: To be recompensed is to be compensated for loss, which is what being indemnified means.

clue.text: Left one by a rich heiress

blocks.note: port is the left side of a ship
I is the Roman numeral one
taken as written

explanation.surface: A wealthy heiress left alone by someone.
explanation.walkthrough: Portia is the wealthy heiress of Belmont in The Merchant of Venice.
explanation.definitionFit: Portia inherits a fortune in Shakespeare's play, and suitors must choose caskets to win her.

clue.text: A Society is in street to help

indicators.note: one piece sits in the other, enclosed by it

blocks.note: taken as written
S is the abbreviation for society
St is the abbreviation for street
taken as written

explanation.surface: A charitable society working in the street to help people.
explanation.walkthrough: The street abbreviation splits around the short word: S + IS + T.
explanation.definitionFit: To assist someone is to help them, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Boy round cliff

blocks.note: O is round in shape
a scar is a steep rocky cliff

explanation.surface: A lad walking round a clifftop.
explanation.walkthrough: Scar for a crag or cliff is common in northern English place names.
explanation.definitionFit: Oscar is a boy's name, so it serves as an example of a boy.

clue.text: Some coaches spoil game

indicators.note: some means only part of what follows, so the answer is a run of its letters

blocks.note: a run of letters across the two words

explanation.surface: Some sports coaches ruin the match.
explanation.definitionFit: Chess is a board game for two players, so it is an example of a game.

clue.text: Slash girls with swords

blocks.note: to slash is to cut
lasses are girls

explanation.surface: A pirate attacking with blades drawn.
explanation.definitionFit: Cutlasses are short curved swords associated with sailors and pirates.

clue.text: Correct soldiers in short commercial

indicators.note: one piece is placed in the other, enclosed
short means cut down, giving the abbreviated form

blocks.note: a commercial is an advertisement
soldiers are men in the ranks

explanation.surface: Getting the troops right in a brief TV advert.
explanation.walkthrough: The commercial shortened is AD, which then wraps around the soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: To amend a text is to correct or improve it, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Generate changes in youth

indicators.note: changes means alters, so the word's letters are altered in order

blocks.note: taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: A sociological claim that youth drives change.
explanation.definitionFit: A teenager is a young person aged thirteen to nineteen, so a youth.

clue.text: Sign, say, knocked over by car

indicators.note: something knocked over is turned upside down, so in an across clue it reads back to front

blocks.note: e.g. means for example, 'say'
the Mini is a classic small British car

explanation.surface: A road sign flattened by a passing car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' just places the car next to the reversed piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Gemini, the Twins, is one of the twelve signs of the zodiac.

clue.text: Article on sailor, vice, and drink

blocks.note: AB is an able-bodied seaman
a vice is a sin
the definite article

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece about a sailor's vices and drinking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' puts the article after the other pieces, as if writing about them.
explanation.definitionFit: Absinthe is a strong green anise-flavoured spirit, so it is a kind of drink.

clue.text: Notice slit in garment is good for appearance

blocks.note: an ad is a notice advertising something
a vent is a slit in the back or side of a jacket

explanation.surface: Fashion advice: a vent in a jacket improves its look.
explanation.definitionFit: An advent is an arrival or coming into being, so the appearance of something.
